---
title: Build OpenJammer
description: The contributor and node-author track — the minimal real-time core and the one plugin contract that makes it infinite.
---
import { Card, CardGrid, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

OpenJammer is built around one boundary: **only what must be real-time-safe and
universal lives in the core; anything that can be a plugin stays a plugin.** A
deliberately tiny Rust core (`ojcore`) turns a node graph into sound and blocks for
nothing. *Everything else* — every instrument, effect, and AI-authored DSP node — is
community territory behind one contract: a `PluginManifest` plus one CLAP-shaped
`DspInstance` trait. Built-in DSP and a synth written this morning are the same shape to
the engine.

The same engine runs **native** on the desktop (low latency, VST3 / AU / CLAP hosting)
and compiled to **WebAssembly** in the browser, selected by `OJ_EXECUTOR`. The wire
contract (`OjGraph`, `RtCommand`, `ParamPatch`, `EngineFrame`) lives once in `ojproto`
and crosses the native ↔ browser seam, parity-gated against its TypeScript mirror.
